subject: Discovery follow-up: scheduling technical deep-dive / loop in security & procurement
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@finpath.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery follow-up: scheduling technical deep-dive / loop in security & procurement

Hi Evan —

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps: 

- Recap: you’re evaluating an LLM inference platform for FinPath’s document ingestion & summarization workloads (sensitive PII scope, low-latency needs for UI).
- Goals: a scalable inference stack, predictable unit-cost, and SOC2-ready controls.
- Next step: technical deep-dive + security checklist review (45–60 min).

Proposed slots (PST):
- Tue 12/15 10:00–11:00
- Tue 12/15 14:00–15:00
- Wed 12/16 09:00–10:00

Looping in Priyom (sales engineer) for the technical deep-dive and Laura (manager) so she’s aware of timelines. If there are additional stakeholders (security, procurement, platform), please let me know who to include and I’ll coordinate.

I’ve also attached a one-page SOC2 summary and our product one-pager for context.

Thanks — talk soon,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0134

Attachments: Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf, Redwood-MAP-v1.pdf

From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@finpath.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finpath.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finpath.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: scheduling technical deep-dive / loop in security & procurement

Thanks Marissa — that recap is spot on. Priya (security) and Marcus (procurement) are cc’d — they’ll want to join the session.

Priya: can you confirm whether SOC2 Type II evidence is required for the initial evaluation? If so, please let us know the specific artifacts you need (logs retention, key management, encryption at rest, etc.).

We can do Tue 12/15 14:00–15:00 PST. Marcus also asked if you can share a draft SOW / pricing outline ahead of the meeting so procurement can start internal review.

Evan
Sr PM, Platform Integrations | FinPath
evan.brooks@finpath.com | +1 212-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@finpath.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finpath.com>, Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finpath.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: scheduling technical deep-dive / loop in security & procurement

Great — locking Tue 12/15 14:00–15:00 PST.

Marcus: I’ve attached a draft SOW and a short pricing outline for your review (SOW-draft.docx). Happy to walk through any items during the call.

Priya: attached is a one-page SOC2 summary (Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf). For the call, we can cover:
- Data handling and isolation options (hosted vs dedicated vs private)
- KMS/HSM integrations and key lifecycle
- Audit logs and retention policy
- Network controls and private deployment options

Priyom — can you take the technical deep-dive? We’ll plan 30–40 minutes on architecture, latency/cost tradeoffs, and platform integration points, then 15 minutes for security/procurement Q&A.

Next steps:
1) I’ll send a calendar invite for Tue 12/15 14:00–15:00 PST with the meeting agenda and attachments.
2) Priyom to prepare a short architecture diagram and example throughput numbers based on the scope Evan shared.
3) Marcus to review SOW and flag any procurement-level changes.

Thanks everyone — looking forward to it.

—Marissa

Attachments: SOW-draft.docx, Redwood-SOC2-summary.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@finpath.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: scheduling technical deep-dive / loop in security & procurement

Thanks Marissa — I’m on for Tue at 14:00 PST.

Evan / Priya / Marcus — quick note on what I’ll cover and what I need from you ahead of the call: 
- What I’ll cover (30–40 min): serving topology options (hosted/dedicated/private), typical latency vs batch sizing tradeoffs, KV cache and prefix caching strategies, example cost per 1k tokens, and integration touchpoints (API, auth, telemetry).
- What I need from you:
  • Expected concurrent sessions / peak qps (even rough numbers)
  • Typical request sequence length (avg tokens per request)
  • Any compliance constraints that would require on-prem or dedicated deployment now

I’ll drop a short architecture diagram and sample throughput table into the calendar invite. If Dev (cc’d) can join for platform integration questions that would be great.

See you Tuesday — I’ll be prepared with a few concrete config options and cost examples.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lee <marcus.lee@finpath.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@finpath.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya.rao@finpath.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 14:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: scheduling technical deep-dive / loop in security & procurement

Confirmed — I’ve accepted the calendar invite for 12/15 14:00 PST. Marcus here from procurement — I’ll skim the SOW this afternoon and flag anything that needs legal/procurement review.

Priyom: expected concurrent sessions — we typically see 15–20 concurrent UI sessions in internal staging, with peak spikes up to ~60 during batch processing. Avg request length is ~350 tokens. If there are any sample configs you want me to run by our infra team before the call, let me know.

Priya: happy to coordinate security artifact requests with Redwood.

Thanks everyone — see you on the call.

Marcus
Senior Procurement Manager | FinPath
marcus.lee@finpath.com
